title: Man who lost $308,000 on sports bets sues Kalshi for offering illegal gambling
author: Jon Brodkin
summary_long: A man who lost over $308,000 making sports wagers on Kalshi is suing the prediction market for violating the state of Washington's ban on online gambling. He's trying to turn those losses into an overall victory with a lawsuit seeking a payment of over $580,000. Bellevue, Washington, resident Scott Bright's "wagering occurred at a time when it was unlawful in Washington and when the Washington Attorney General had already sued KalshiEX LLC in this Court alleging precisely that," said the gambler's lawsuit filed on September 24 in King County Superior Court. Kalshi has since filed a motion to dismiss the lawsuit. Source: arstechnica.com. Date: 2026-11-09. Why it matters: outline likely impact on technology, business, or society. title: Vulnerability that lets hackers SSH into Linux devices is under active exploitation
author: Dan Goodin
summary_long: Hackers are actively exploiting a recently discovered critical vulnerability that allows them to log in to privileged accounts on many Linux systems, multiple researchers are reporting. The vulnerability, tracked under the name *sshole, arises from the interaction between OpenSSH and a code library known as musl. Linux systems that use both of these packages and meet certain other requirements can be hacked to give unauthenticated access to high-privilege accounts in a matter of seconds. *sshole became publicly known last Thursday and quickly stoked concerns it could lead to widespread compromise of Linux machines. Source: arstechnica.com. Date: 2026-11-09. Why it matters: outline likely impact on technology, business, or society. What’s next: note near-term developments or signals to watch.
